raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Streaming chat now drops tool calls in the same cases batch does. Fixes #63346. Follow-up to #63148 which listed this as not covered.

#42752 fixed #42747 for `"none"` but only inside `DelegatingParser`. Two cases still slip through on main:

- gpt-oss with `"none"`: `HarmonyParser` isn't a `DelegatingParser` so the guard never runs.
- `null` with any parser: nothing gates it, so streaming keeps tool calls while batch drops them.

This PR moves the rule into one place that batch and streaming both call, so it no longer depends on each parser.

## Claims

- With `stream: true`, `/v1/chat/completions` now follows the same `tool_choice` rules as batch. gpt-oss (Harmony) with `"none"` and any tool parser with `null` stop returning tool calls. This PR doesn't decide what `null` should mean, it only makes streaming match batch.
- Streaming `/v1/chat/completions/derender` gets the same fix because it uses the same `ChatStreamProcessor`.
- `finish_reason` is `stop` in those cases, not `tool_calls`.
- No change for `"auto"`, `"required"` or named tools. Anthropic and Cohere turn `null` into `"auto"` when tools are set, so they're not affected.

## Validation

Reproduced before the fix at main `ccd4e4030f`, `temperature: 0` with the `auto` row as a control:

```text
--- gpt-oss-20b (openai parser), tool_choice="none"
  chat stream (auto)   tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
  chat batch           tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  chat stream          tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
  derender batch       tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender stream      tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls

--- Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (hermes), tool_choice=null
  chat stream (auto)   tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
  chat batch           tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  chat stream          tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
  derender batch       tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender stream      tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
```

After the fix:

```text
--- gpt-oss-20b (openai parser), tool_choice="none"
  chat stream (auto)   tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
  chat batch           tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  chat stream          tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender batch       tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender stream      tool_calls=[]               finish=stop

--- Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (hermes), tool_choice=null
  chat stream (auto)   tool_calls=['get_weather']  finish=tool_calls
  chat batch           tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  chat stream          tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender batch       tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender stream      tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
```

The `auto` control still streams the tool call which means nothing extra is dropped.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_stream_processor.py \
tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_message_assembly.py \
tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py \
tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py \
tests/tool_use/mistral/test_mistral_tool_calls.py -v
```

New and changed tests:

- `test_drops_tool_calls_like_non_streaming`: `"none"` and `null`, with a mixed content and tool call delta and a tool call only delta.
- `test_e2e_harmony_tool_choice_none_drops_tool_calls`: now also runs with `stream: true` against the real gpt-oss render server.
- `test_derender_stream.py`: the `_FakeParser` fixture now has auto tools on. One test sent no tools with the default `tool_choice: "none"` and still expected tool calls, so it relied on this bug. It now sends `"auto"`.

No model eval. Generation doesn't change, only which parsed fields are returned.

No docs change. `tool_calling.md` already says `"none"` returns no tool calls.

## Details

`ChatStreamProcessor` passed `parse_delta()` output straight through and relied on the parser to check `tool_choice`. Not every parser does. `HarmonyParser` ignores `"none"` and the base `Parser` treats `null` like `"auto"`. Non-streaming doesn't have this problem because `assemble_chat_message_fields()` applies the rule itself.

The rule now lives in `keeps_tool_calls()` and both paths call it. `ChatStreamProcessor` takes `enable_auto_tools` and `parser_cls` as required keyword arguments, so a new caller can't skip them by accident.

When tool calls are dropped, the stream sends nothing for them. That matches batch which returns `content: ""`. Whether `"none"` should return tool-call-shaped text as content is #55080 and this PR doesn't change that. If a delta is empty after stripping, the processor returns `None`. Both callers already skip sending a `None` delta, the same way they handle hidden reasoning.

## Related PRs

- #42752 (merged): gates `"none"` in `DelegatingParser` only. This PR covers what that misses.
- #42868: targets the old `serving.py` streaming code which has since moved to `ChatStreamProcessor`. Obsolete and conflicting.
- #55089 / #55080: whether tool-call-shaped text should come back as content when tools are off. Out of scope here.
- #54321: makes an explicit `null` behave like an omitted field, so `"auto"` when tools are set. Complementary to this PR. If it lands, both paths follow it.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [ ] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [ ] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

nodes.body: Hmm I remember seeing similar PRs before, could you check for duplicate PRs?

Related open work worth cross-linking: #42868 bypasses parsing in the older serving path, #55089 preserves raw text when tool calling is off, and #54321 normalizes explicit null to the omitted-field default. This patch instead matches current batch filtering after parsing. That distinction matters for null; this is a bounded overlap check, not exhaustive duplicate clearance.

An independent AI-assisted CPU check used real ChatCompletionRequest constructors and Hermes/DelegatingParser through the complete stream/batch modules, with offline byte-level BPE. At 325fb35 versus ccd4e40, eight null/tool-call stream cases disagreed with batch before and agree after, including last-chunk and empty-EOS finishing. The other 40 controls, batch outputs and token counts stayed unchanged. All seven checked source blobs also match 24a35ea. Dependencies were vLLM 0.32 / Torch 2.13; this does not verify the full current tree, Harmony, real model weights, HTTP/derender services or CI.

Thanks @DarkLight1337 and @adenzhou1350 for "heads up". I should have linked these: #42747 was fixed by #42752 which gates `"none"` inside `DelegatingParser.parse_delta`. That leaves two streaming gaps, both reproduced on current main in the PR description:

- `HarmonyParser` (gpt-oss) isn't a `DelegatingParser`, so `"none"` still streams tool calls.
- `tool_choice: null` isn't gated by any parser, so it streams tool calls while batch drops them.

This PR moves the rule into `keeps_tool_calls()` which batch and streaming both call, instead of relying on each parser.

Other open PRs:
- #42868 targets the old `serving.py` streaming code which has since moved to `ChatStreamProcessor`. It's obsolete and has merge conflicts.
- #55089 (#55080) is about returning tool-call-shaped text as content when tools are off. That's out of scope here.
- #54321 makes an explicit `null` behave like an omitted field (`"auto" `with tools). It's complementary. This PR only makes streaming match batch, so if #54321 lands, both paths follow it.

@adenzhou1350 thanks for the independent check. I also updated the title and description to be more explicit.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

**Code review found no issues**

No high-confidence issues detected in this change.

issue_comments.body: Hmm I remember seeing similar PRs before, could you check for duplicate PRs?

Related open work worth cross-linking: #42868 bypasses parsing in the older serving path, #55089 preserves raw text when tool calling is off, and #54321 normalizes explicit null to the omitted-field default. This patch instead matches current batch filtering after parsing. That distinction matters for null; this is a bounded overlap check, not exhaustive duplicate clearance.

An independent AI-assisted CPU check used real ChatCompletionRequest constructors and Hermes/DelegatingParser through the complete stream/batch modules, with offline byte-level BPE. At 325fb35 versus ccd4e40, eight null/tool-call stream cases disagreed with batch before and agree after, including last-chunk and empty-EOS finishing. The other 40 controls, batch outputs and token counts stayed unchanged. All seven checked source blobs also match 24a35ea. Dependencies were vLLM 0.32 / Torch 2.13; this does not verify the full current tree, Harmony, real model weights, HTTP/derender services or CI.

Thanks @DarkLight1337 and @adenzhou1350 for "heads up". I should have linked these: #42747 was fixed by #42752 which gates `"none"` inside `DelegatingParser.parse_delta`. That leaves two streaming gaps, both reproduced on current main in the PR description:

- `HarmonyParser` (gpt-oss) isn't a `DelegatingParser`, so `"none"` still streams tool calls.
- `tool_choice: null` isn't gated by any parser, so it streams tool calls while batch drops them.

This PR moves the rule into `keeps_tool_calls()` which batch and streaming both call, instead of relying on each parser.

Other open PRs:
- #42868 targets the old `serving.py` streaming code which has since moved to `ChatStreamProcessor`. It's obsolete and has merge conflicts.
- #55089 (#55080) is about returning tool-call-shaped text as content when tools are off. That's out of scope here.
- #54321 makes an explicit `null` behave like an omitted field (`"auto" `with tools). It's complementary. This PR only makes streaming match batch, so if #54321 lands, both paths follow it.

@adenzhou1350 thanks for the independent check. I also updated the title and description to be more explicit.
